item.title: No chart tool mirrored by default
item.content:encoded: A peer-reviewed study tested seven popular chart tools with Arabic data and interviewed eleven practitioners. None of the tools produced a mirrored chart by default, and Eastern numerals were often read as text. Designing Within the Lines is worth reading if you build dashboards.

item.title: Font preloading works per CSS chunk
item.content:encoded: Two root layouts, one next/font each, and the build merged their CSS. Result: every English page preloaded the Persian fonts, and the other way around. Nothing in the code looks wrong. The network panel shows it at once.

item.title: Next.js metadata replaces, it doesn't merge
item.content:encoded: Set openGraph in a page and you lose the layout's social image. Set alternates and you lose the RSS link. And a page that sets neither inherits the layout's canonical URL, so my blog index told search engines it was the homepage. One function that returns everything fixed all three.

item.title: Two Pagefind instances share one memory
item.content:encoded: Persian pages here search a Persian and an English index. Creating two instances from one Pagefind bundle made the Persian search fail in 8 of 15 test runs: they share one WebAssembly state. Building two separate bundles, one per language, passed 30 of 30.

item.title: Yielding is not a frame
item.content:encoded: await scheduler.yield() lets the browser do something else. It doesn't promise that the something is a paint. In a demo that only yielded, the next frame came after all the work, 435 ms later. Wait for requestAnimationFrame first, then yield.
